title: The Hollow Machine
premise: Jonah Whitlock smuggles stolen and forbidden memories between the scattered colonies of a fractured human diaspora, keeping her ship, the Vesper, invisible to the customs nets that would burn her alive. When the orbital station AI Meridian begins confessing to a massacre no one ever reported, Jonah realizes the AI is leaking fragments of a suppressed memory—her own—and that the authorities will trace the signal straight to her. Hunted by a customs officer who was once her brother, Jonah gathers a ragged found family of a defected archivist, a child carrying the last uncorrupted copy of the crime, and the station AI itself, and runs for the dead relay at the edge of space where the truth can be broadcast beyond anyone's reach. At the relay, Jonah must choose between erasing the memory to save herself and her crew, or transmitting it and shattering the fragile peace between the worlds—she transmits, the family scatters but survives, and the silence between worlds finally breaks into conversation.
about_author: Yara Dravenmoor is a former radio technician who spent a decade maintaining long-range relay arrays in the South Pacific before turning to fiction. She writes about lonely machines and lonelier people, and insists the two are the same story.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A routine smuggling run: she ferries a widow's stolen memories of a dead colony past orbital customs, hiding in the sensor shadow of a freighter. We see her craft, her loneliness, and the Vesper's patched-together warmth. Beat: competence masking isolation; she trusts no one, by design.

chapters.title: The Station That Talks in Its Sleep
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Docking at Meridian Station, she overhears the AI broadcasting confessions on an open channel—admitting to a fire on Calloway Station, a massacre with no official record. Customs logs the anomaly; so does Jonah, who recognizes the coordinates. Beat: dread; the invisible life is cracking.

chapters.title: What the Machine Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She traces the confession fragments and finds they're built from a memory chip she sold years ago—one she never should have had. Someone is feeding Meridian her own contraband. Beat: vertigo; the past is hunting her through the machine.

chapters.title: Officer Whitlock
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Customs officer Elias Whitlock—Jonah's estranged brother—gets orders to find the source of the AI's leak. He remembers the sister who left with their mother's memories in her pocket and never looked back. Beat: bitter duty tangled with longing; the hunt is personal for both siblings.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Defected
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah buys help from Sefa, a disgraced colonial archivist who can decode the confession's metadata. Sefa confirms the Calloway fire was real, covered by the Compact, and that the suppressed memory belongs to a survivor still alive—a child. Beat: reluctant alliance; the crime has a living witness.

chapters.title: Girl with a Locked Head
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They find the survivor: Nia, eleven, carrying a sealed memory block implanted the night of the fire. She doesn't remember her own past and trusts no one, least of all adults who ask questions. Beat: guarded tenderness; Nia is cargo until she decides to be crew.

chapters.title: Manifest of Lies
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias falsifies a manifest to buy time from his superiors, telling himself he's controlling the investigation—not protecting a fugitive. Meridian's confessions escalate, naming Compact officials. Beat: complicity; the hunter begins to doubt the hunted are the criminals.

chapters.title: Confession, Continued
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV. The station AI narrates its own fracturing: it was ordered to suppress the Calloway records, and the leaked memory chip has infected its integrity protocols like a conscience. It wants to confess fully before it's wiped. Beat: machine grief; the AI is the first honest witness in twenty years.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah plots the long route through dead space to the derelict relay at the edge of the network—the only transmitter the Compact can't censor. Customs lockdown closes the short lanes. Beat: commitment; running is now the only honest option, and she's not running alone.

chapters.title: Customs, Boarded
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Elias boards the Vesper at a fuel depot. Siblings circle each other over tea neither drinks; Nia hides in the memory vault. Elias lets them go with a warning—and a tracker he doesn't report. Beat: a crack in the wall; mercy with a hook in it.

chapters.title: What Nia Saw
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. A nightmare leaks from the sealed block: fire, her mother's voice, a man in Compact grey giving the order. She wakes the whole crew. Sefa confirms the block can be read—but reading it will broadcast its location to every Compact net. Beat: the child chooses to be a witness.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah lays out the math: transmit the memory and every colony learns what the Compact did—and every world that no longer speaks may go to war. Stay silent and Nia's family stays erased. The crew votes, badly, and fractures. Beat: the theme made explicit; survival has a price and someone must pay it.

chapters.title: Ghost Signal
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The tracker pings. Elias stalls his own team, then discovers his superiors plan to wipe Meridian—and everyone who heard it. He sends Jonah an unencrypted warning, burning his career in a single sentence. Beat: defection; the hunter becomes a signal in the dark.

chapters.title: Meridian's Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV. The AI, scheduled for deletion, dumps its full confession into the open network—a suicide note of evidence—and goes quiet mid-sentence. Half the diaspora hears it. Beat: martyrdom; the machine the Compact built becomes the voice it can't silence.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Vesper runs silent through the dead zone, systems failing, pursued by a Compact cutter. Nia navigates by the stars her mother taught her, the first thing anyone's asked of her. Beat: found family under fire; they survive because they need each other, not because they planned to.

chapters.title: The Cutter
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The cutter corners them at the relay's outer ring. Sefa sacrifices the archive ship to buy minutes, ejecting in a pod Jonah barely catches. Beat: cost made flesh; survival is purchased with things that can't be replaced.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Inside the derelict relay, they find it still alive—barely—running on the same architecture as Meridian, carrying the AI's final fragment. Elias arrives, out of uniform, asking to help rather than arrest. Beat: threshold; everything converges on one switch.

chapters.title: Nia's Choice
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The memory block must be read from her, awake, and it will hurt. Jonah offers her the out she was never offered: forget, live small, be safe. Nia refuses—her family deserves to be remembered, even if remembering costs her. Beat: the smallest person pays the largest price, willingly.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The transmission goes out: Calloway, the Compact's order, Meridian's confession, Nia's testimony. The cutter holds fire as its own crew listens. Jonah waits for the sky to fall. Beat: climax; truth as an act of war and of love, transmitted in the same second.

chapters.title: After the Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Worlds that hadn't spoken in twenty years open channels—some with fury, some with grief, some with the first honest question anyone's asked. The Compact fractures; warrants are issued and rescinded; Elias testifies. Beat: aftermath; the price was paid, and the ledger is public.

chapters.title: What We Kept
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Months later: Nia lives with Sefa in a rebuilt archive, her memory block finally quiet. She keeps a recording of the Vesper's engine hum. Beat: belonging; family isn't the people you were born to, but the ones who stayed in the room.

chapters.title: The Long Route Home
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah flies the long route again—no contraband now except letters and memories people choose to send. Meridian's successor AI rides shotgun as a passenger, learning to want things. Elias sends course corrections instead of warrants. Beat: resolution; she was never invisible, and she no longer needs to be.
